abstract: Rhizoctonia solani AG1-IB is an economically important fungal pathogen of turfgrass and agricultural crops, yet available genome assemblies remain fragmented or represent collapsed or consensus sequences that obscure haplotype-specific variation, limiting investigations of genome evolution and heterokaryosis. Here, we present a chromosome-scale, haplotype-aware genome assembly of AG1-IB isolate S1W6 generated using Oxford Nanopore sequencing, Hi-C scaffolding, and short-read polishing. De novo assembly with PECAT produced two haplotype-aware nuclear genome assemblies, with BUSCO completeness greater than 96% and nuclear genome N50 values exceeding 2 Mb. Comparative analyses revealed substantial haplotype divergence, with over 600,000 SNPs and 80,000 indels between haplotypes with 97.75% average nucleotide identity separating assemblies. FastANI analyses showed comparable genetic divergence between Hap1 and Hap2 assemblies of S1W6 to that observed among independently collected AG1-IB isolates from different plant hosts and geographic regions. Despite extensive nucleotide variation, Gene Ontology profiles, predicted effector repertoires, carbohydrate-active enzymes, and biosynthetic gene cluster composition were conserved between assemblies. In contrast, homeodomain (HD) mating-type loci were variable. Hap2 contained four HD genes (W-HD1, W-HD2, E-HD1, and E-HD2), whereas Hap1 lacked E-HD1, and shared divergent HD amino acid sequences. A STE3 pheromone receptor gene on chromosome 15 was highly conserved in both haplotypes. This study provides the first chromosome-scale, haplotype-resolved genome resource for R. solani AG1-IB and demonstrates that heterokaryotic individuals can harbor genomic variation approaching the levels observed among genetically diverse isolates of AG1-IB. These findings highlight the importance of haplotype-aware assemblies for understanding genome evolution and mating-type diversity in heterokaryotic fungal plant pathogens.
